Elon Musk quickly impressed Franz von Holzhausen, persuading him to join Tesla and leave behind a successful career at Mazda. Franz recalls: "For somebody who's going to put rockets into space, car is actually not that hard, and his vision for the car and his sustainable direction and message is exactly what I'm looking for."

In the summer of 2008, Franz already had the kind of automotive career most designers dream about, having penned sports cars at GM and led design at Mazda North America, while Tesla was near bankruptcy. 

But after meeting Elon Musk at SpaceX and going for a drive together in an early Roadster while people on the street stopped to stare, Franz walked away from his secure job to start designing the Model S from a blank sheet of paper. When he later explained why he took that leap of faith into a startup with no guarantees, his answer came down to Elon's total commitment: "Tesla was all in."

retweet.text:
JUST IN: ~70% of signers on the petition against SpaceX's data center in Arizona's Cochise County don't even live there, according to Supervisor Kathleen Gomez

"I went on to that. There was one where you just signed your name. You didn't even have to say your address or where you're from. Then there was another one by change[.]org, and there's at least 60% of those people are not from Cochise County."

"I have a real problem with people outside of our county trying to tell us what we should do and what we shouldn't do. My family goes back over since the eighteen eighties. I do not wanna ruin Cochise County. I do not wanna make it worse. In fact, that would be something that would horrify me."

"So, you know, the people at Cochise County, we're smart people. We know what we're doing. We know what we want for our vision, and we pass a comprehensive plan that's really thorough on everything. I would say to people, if you had the time like I did and went and checked each one of those signatures, you're gonna see that so many are not from Cochise County, like, at least 60% to even 70."

"So to me, I'm talking to the people on the street. I'm talking to the organizations that I meet, and that's where I'm gonna make my decision from what I hear from the people."
